content:
Ethan Park: Heads up: for the incident taxonomy project, we need to expose `incident_type` + `subtype` in the internal APIs that Console uses (ops views) so CS can reference it for comms. Key constraint from SRE: CS should be able to *view* but not modify any classification fields.

Marissa Cole: +1. From Product side: we want CS to see type/owner + high-level status, but we cannot have accidental edits that change reporting / owner mapping.

Dylan Brooks: how are we thinking about the write path today? is Console directly patching incident records or does it go via incident-bot / incident service?

Ethan Park: current state: incident-bot writes classification into incident svc, Console ops can also update some incident fields via an internal endpoint (`PATCH /internal/incidents/:id`). The `incident_type` addition is in PR-28503 but permissioning is not settled.

Rachel Kim: CS needs read-only. Ideally no edit affordance in UI, but also enforce at API level so you can’t call it with a token.

Dev Patel: for CS workflows, we mainly need: incident id, current severity, affected tier (Hosted/Dedicated/Private), incident_type/subtype, owner team, and any customer-facing status page link. We do NOT need to change classification.

Allison Grant: please don’t forget about audit. If type is being displayed to CS, we should log access at least at the API gateway / auth layer. Not necessarily per-view, but don’t make it totally dark.

Sergio Costa: also, are we surfacing `unknown/unclassified`? if CS sees that, they’ll ask what it means. might be fine but we should label it clearly.

Ethan Park: proposal:
1) Add read-only fields to `GET /internal/incidents/:id` and list endpoints.
2) Gate all mutation of `incident_type`, `subtype`, and `owner_team` behind a new permission `incident.classification:write`.
3) CS role gets `incident:read` but not classification:write.

Dylan Brooks: would that break existing Console ops users? what roles do they have today?

Ethan Park: ops (SRE/oncall) uses `ops-admin` role via Okta group. We can attach `incident.classification:write` to ops-admin. CS group stays on `cs-ops` role.

Marissa Cole: are there any other fields CS currently edits? I think they can add internal notes?

Ethan Park: yep. we’re not touching notes/comments right now, just classification.

Rachel Kim: I want to make sure the read-only view includes the resolved owner mapping as well. There’s confusion when type is set but owner mapping changes later.

Ethan Park: good call. We can return both:
- `classification`: incident_type/subtype (what was set)
- `resolved_owner`: derived from control plane mapping version at read time
But need to be careful w/ reporting consistency.

Allison Grant: if you return `resolved_owner`, include `owner_mapping_version` so people know why it changed. Otherwise it’ll look like the owner is flapping.

Devon Price: (jumping in from incident-bot side) FYI incident-bot uses the incident svc write endpoint w/ a service token. If we add the permission check, make sure the service token has it. Otherwise taxonomy selection will start failing next week :grimacing:

Ethan Park: yep, service token will get `incident.classification:write`. We’ll enforce based on token claims not user-agent.

Dylan Brooks: implementation idea: don’t overload existing PATCH endpoint w/ partial perms. Create a dedicated endpoint for classification updates:
`PUT /internal/incidents/:id/classification`
Then we can gate the whole endpoint with classification:write and keep old PATCH for other fields.

Marissa Cole: +1. Easier to reason about; also makes it simpler for Console UI (only ops sees the classification edit panel, CS sees read-only). 

Rachel Kim: also helps with comms training: “CS can’t update classification, only on-call/incident commander can.”

Sergio Costa: what about the status page snippet templates by type? CS will want a stable string. Are we returning raw enums or display names?

Ethan Park: API should return enums + a display label, but label is for UI only. Something like:
```
incident_type: "ROUTING_FALLBACK"
incident_subtype: "POLICY_MISCONFIG"
incident_type_label: "Routing / fallback"
incident_subtype_label: "Policy misconfiguration"
```
We can also return `runbook_url` but that might be ops-only.

Dev Patel: runbook URL is fine to keep hidden from CS. We mostly need the plain language labels.

Allison Grant: careful on cardinality: don’t add a field that can be arbitrary text. Labels should come from the same allowlist table as the enums.

Ethan Park: agreed. We’ll keep labels server-side based on allowlist.

Dylan Brooks: permission model detail: if CS uses Console, they authenticate via user token. But support tooling sometimes uses a shared “cs-tools” service token. Make sure that token also cannot mutate classification.

Rachel Kim: yes please. We’ve had issues before where a service token had broad perms “just for convenience”.

Ethan Park: action items:
- [Ethan] Update PR-28503 to add GET fields + new `PUT /classification` endpoint.
- [Ethan] Add RBAC check: `incident.classification:write` required for the classification endpoint.
- [Dylan] Confirm current roles/groups: `ops-admin`, `cs-ops`, `cs-tools` and what claims they map to.
- [Marissa/Rachel] Confirm what fields CS should see in Console v1 (type/subtype, owner, tier, severity, status page link).

Marissa Cole: for CS view, include “last updated by” and “last updated at” for classification if possible. Helps with escalation when they see it change.

Ethan Park: can do. We already store `updated_by` on incident updates; for classification specifically we can record `classification_updated_by` + `classification_updated_at` to avoid ambiguity.

Devon Price: please ping me before merging if there’s any schema change; incident-bot’s modal might start showing blanks if field names change.

Ethan Park: will do.

Dylan Brooks: one more: do we need to prevent CS from editing via GraphQL (if Console uses it)?

Ethan Park: Console uses REST for incidents today. If/when GraphQL comes back, same permission gate. We’ll put the enforcement in incident svc so it’s not bypassable.

Sergio Costa: timeline? SRE wants this rolled out with the taxonomy required-fields enforcement.

Ethan Park: aiming to merge by EOW, behind a feature flag `incident_taxonomy_readonly_cs`. Can enable for CS group first to validate, then general.

Rachel Kim: sounds good. Please add a short note to the rollout doc: “CS can view taxonomy fields; changes must be requested in #incidents via IC/on-call.”

Ethan Park: yep.

Allison Grant: (last nit) if you add access logging, keep it lightweight. We don’t want to create a new giant log stream that itself becomes a reliability incident :)

Ethan Park: lol. We’ll stick to standard gateway audit events + sampling.

Marissa Cole: thanks all. keep me looped on the PR changes so we can align with Console surfacing.

Ethan Park: will post the updated PR link here once ready.
